transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose I’ve been feeling low enough that it started to worry me. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, because I’m not planning to do anything to myself, but some mornings I wake up and think… it might have been easier if I just hadn’t woken up. That scared me a bit, and I thought I should probably talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About a month, I think. It seemed to start after my sister died unexpectedly. I know grief is normal, of course, so I didn’t want to overreact… but it’s been lingering since then.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities that you usually enjoy?

Yes… I suppose I have, though I still try to keep up with things. I go to book club and the dance night and all that, because I don’t want to just sit at home, but lately I’m sort of… there without really being there. Like I’m watching through a pane of glass, if that makes sense.

Even my garden, and cooking little things for the neighbors—those usually give me a lift, but lately they don’t seem to do much. I still do them, mostly, but it feels flatter than it used to.
Have you been experiencing a lack of energy or feeling fatigued, even after getting enough rest?

Yes… a bit, I think. I mean, I do manage what I need to do, so it’s not as though I’m completely laid up or anything. But even simple errands seem to take it out of me lately. Or getting the papers together for the Cultural Center—I’ll do it, but afterward I feel worn out, like my body’s moving through thick mud. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently?

A little, yes… nothing dramatic, I don’t think. Food just doesn’t seem to call to me much lately. I’ll make myself some toast or a bowl of soup, and then by the evening I’ll realize I’ve barely eaten. I’m not trying to lose weight or anything… it just sort of slips by me.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

I don’t think so… not in any obvious way, anyway. I’m maybe a little slower getting going, but I wouldn’t say people would notice me shuffling about or anything like that. And I’m not really pacing or unable to sit still.

Is that all right—does that answer what you mean?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately, or perhaps feeling like you’re not worth much?

I suppose… yes, a little. I don’t want to make it sound overly dramatic, but I do keep going back over the last weeks with my sister. I find myself thinking I should have called more, or listened better, or somehow done something more useful.

Part of me knows I probably couldn’t have changed what happened, but I still keep turning it over and blaming myself. Does that make sense?
Have you had any other thoughts about death or dying lately, or found yourself wishing you weren’t here anymore?

I… yes, a little. I’m sorry, that sounds awful to say.

I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, and I don’t think I would do anything like that. But some mornings I wake up and there’s this thought that it might have been easier if I just hadn’t woken up at all. That’s really what frightened me enough to come and ask for help.

Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
How often do you find yourself unable to enjoy or engage in activities, even when you make an effort, and does this happen almost every day or only occasionally?

It’s… more days than not, I think. I do still make myself go to things — book club, and the dance night — so I’m not just sitting at home all the time.

But even when I’m there, I feel a bit like I’m behind a pane of glass, if that makes sense. I’m present, but not really… taking it in. And things that usually give me a little lift, like being in the garden or cooking something for the neighbors, just don’t seem to do that lately.

I don’t know if I’d say every single day, but it’s close to that. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking?
Have you noticed that even small tasks, like getting dressed or making a phone call, take much more effort than they used to, or do you feel like you're moving through life in slow motion?

Yes… I think so. Not terribly, maybe, but it’s noticeable.

Even simple errands seem to take it out of me more than they used to. Or if I’m getting papers together for the Cultural Center, which shouldn’t be a big thing, I end up feeling worn out afterward. It’s like my body is moving through thick mud, if that makes sense.

I can still do things, mostly, but it all feels like much more effort than it ought to.
Have you noticed that your thoughts are slowed down, or that it’s harder to think or make decisions than usual?

A little, yes. I mean, I’m still managing, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But I’ve noticed I’ll sit with the same budgeting spreadsheet and just… stare at it, or I’ll reread a paragraph for the workshop three or four times and still not really take in what it says. Then I feel silly, because it’s not difficult material. It’s just harder to make my mind settle on it.

Is that what you mean by slowed down?
Would you say that these feelings tend to be worse at a particular time of day, or do they stay about the same throughout the day?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clear pattern, honestly. I don’t think I could say, “Oh, it’s always worse in the morning,” or anything like that.

It seems to sort of hover in the background through the day. Some moments are better than others, depending on what I’m doing, but I haven’t tracked it closely. Should I be paying more attention to that?
Have you lost any noticeable amount of weight recently, even without trying to?

A little, maybe. I haven’t been trying to lose weight or anything.

It’s more that food just doesn’t really call to me much lately. I’ll make something small, like toast or a bit of soup, and then by the evening I realize I’ve hardly eaten. I don’t think it’s dramatic, but… yes, I suppose it’s noticeable. Does that count?
Have you found that nothing gives you pleasure anymore, even things you used to really enjoy?

I wouldn’t say nothing, exactly… I still go to things. I make myself show up for book club, and there’s a dance night I used to really look forward to.

But lately I’m sort of just… there. Like I’m sitting behind a pane of glass watching everyone else enjoy it. Even my garden, or cooking something for the neighbors, those used to give me a little lift, and now they don’t really seem to. I feel bad saying that, because I know I’m lucky to have those things. Does that make sense?
